## Setup

Run `01_clean.R` first. It reads the Google Sheet output, stacks the 13 team tabs, and saves `data/team_games.csv`. Everything here starts from that file.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

team_games <- read_csv("data/team_games.csv")
games      <- read_csv("data/games.csv")

glimpse(team_games)
```

`team_games` has one row per team per game. A conference game therefore appears twice, once from each side. `games` has one row per conference match.

## The xG measure

The weights live in one place, so changing them changes everything below.

```{r}
w_on_target  <- 0.246   # value of a shot on target
w_off_target <- 0.070   # value of a shot that missed or was blocked
draw_margin  <- 0.5     # |xG difference| smaller than this = predicted draw

est_xg <- function(sot, shots_off) {
  sot * w_on_target + shots_off * w_off_target
}
```

One `mutate()` replaces the 13 copied blocks:

```{r}
team_games <- team_games |>
  mutate(
    xg_for     = est_xg(sot_for, shots_off_for),
    xg_against = est_xg(sot_against, shots_off_against),
    xg_diff    = xg_for - xg_against,
    x_result   = case_when(
      xg_diff >=  draw_margin ~ "W",
      xg_diff <= -draw_margin ~ "L",
      TRUE                    ~ "D"))
```

## How good is it?

### Season totals by team

```{r}
team_summary <- team_games |>
  group_by(team) |>
  summarise(
    games       = n(),
    points      = sum(points),
    goals_for   = sum(goals_for),
    xg_for      = sum(xg_for),
    goals_minus_xg = goals_for - xg_for,
    goals_against  = sum(goals_against),
    xg_against     = sum(xg_against),
    goals_against_minus_xg_against = goals_against - xg_against) |>
  arrange(desc(points))

team_summary

team_summary |>
  mutate(gap = (goals_for - goals_against) - (xg_for - xg_against),
         team = fct_reorder(team, gap)) |>
  ggplot(aes(gap, team, fill = gap > 0)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#1b6ca8", `FALSE` = "#d1495b")) +
  labs(x = "Goal difference minus xG difference", y = NULL,
       title = "Who over- or under-performed their shots?")
```

-   Over 10 goal over performance in goals_minus_xg for Point Loma

-   Over 6 goal under performance in goals_minus_xg for Jessup

-   Over 14 goal under performance in goals_against_minus_xg_against for Jessup

-   Over 6.5 goal over performance in goals_against_minus_xg_against for Chaminade

-   Over 4.5 goal over performance in goals_against_minus_xg_against for Vanguard

-   Point Loma'a goal difference was +24, its xG diff was only 11.4, Gap of +12.6

-   Vanguards goal difference was +13, its xG diff was only 5.9, Gap of +7.1

-   Chaminades goal difference was -13, its xG diff was -20, Gap of +7.0

-   Jessup's goal difference was -32, its xG diff was –11.9, Gap of -20.1

-   Biola and Westmont both had gaps of around -5, pretty big but nothing extreme

-   This shows both how lucky or unlucky teams likely got over the season, but can also potentially show information we can not access, such as Jessup giving up better quality chances on average per shot, or Point Loma creating better quality chances on average per shot. Or teams that had a positive gap giving up lower quality shots.

```{r}
ggplot(team_summary, aes(xg_for, goals_for, label = team)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(vjust = -0.8, size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Estimated xG", y = "Actual goals",
       title = "Goals vs. estimated xG, season totals",
       subtitle = "Teams above the line scored more than their shots predict")

```

### Game by game

```{r}
matches <- read_csv("data/games.csv") |>
  mutate(
    home_xg  = est_xg(home_sot, home_shots - home_sot),
    away_xg  = est_xg(away_sot, away_shots - away_sot),
    xg_diff  = home_xg - away_xg,
    x_result = case_when(xg_diff >=  draw_margin ~ "W",
                         xg_diff <= -draw_margin ~ "L",
                         TRUE                    ~ "D"))

tab <- table(Actual    = factor(matches$home_result, c("W", "D", "L"), c("Win", "Draw", "Loss")),
             Predicted = factor(matches$x_result,    c("W", "D", "L"), c("Win", "Draw", "Loss")))
addmargins(tab)
```

Accuracy is **36 of 65, or 55.4%**. That is the same percentage as before, as expected, since the earlier table was just this one doubled up.

The model called the right side in 33 of the 38 games where it picked a winner (87%). It also labeled 22 games as draws when only 8 games ended in draws, and that is where most of the accuracy is lost.

```{r}
ggplot(team_games, aes(xg_for, goals_for)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.1, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "Estimated xG", y = "Goals", title = "Goals vs. estimated xG, single games")
```

## Where this goes next

### 1. Where do 0.246 and 0.070 come from?

-   If they were calcualted to fit the 2025 season, how do you know they aren't just describing the results of 2025? Is it generalizable?
-   Fit them instead of picking them. How close are the fitted weights to yours? How wide are their confidence intervals?

```{r}
m <- glm(goals_for ~ 0 + sot_for + shots_off_for, family = poisson(link = "identity"), data   = team_games)

summary(m)


# Learn the two weights from one set of games
fit_xg <- function(train) {
  coef(lm(goals_for ~ 0 + sot_for + shots_off_for, data = train))
}

# Apply those weights to a different set of games and score them
test_xg <- function(test, w, train, draw_margin = 0.5) {
  test |>
    mutate(
      xg_for     = w[1] * sot_for     + w[2] * shots_off_for,
      xg_against = w[1] * sot_against + w[2] * shots_off_against,
      x_result   = case_when(xg_for - xg_against >=  draw_margin ~ "W",
                             xg_for - xg_against <= -draw_margin ~ "L",
                             TRUE ~ "D")) |>
    summarise(
      games           = n(),
      actual_goals    = sum(goals_for),
      predicted_goals = sum(xg_for),
      error_per_game  = sqrt(mean((goals_for - xg_for)^2)),
      # baseline: guess the training games' average for every game
      baseline_error  = sqrt(mean((goals_for - mean(train$goals_for))^2)),
      result_accuracy = mean(result == x_result))
}

# Example: learn from each team's first 5 games, test on its last 5
train <- filter(team_games, game_no <= 5)
test  <- filter(team_games, game_no >  5)

w <- fit_xg(train)
w
test_xg(test, w, train)

# Vlad's own weights on the same test games, for comparison
print(test_xg(test, c(0.33, 0.15), train))

```

### 2. Does it work on games it hasn't seen?

-   Add the 2023 and 2024 seasons (same tabs, set `SEASON` in `01_clean.R`, stack the three files). Fit on two seasons, test on the third.
-   Compare against simple baselines. What accuracy do you get from "the home team wins"? From "the team with more shots wins"? A model only matters if it beats those.

### 3. Does xG tell you something goals don't?

-   Split the season in half (`game_no` is the order of games on each tab). Which predicts second-half points better: first-half goal difference, or first-half xG difference?
-   Which teams score well above or below their xG? Is that gap stable from the first half to the second, or does it disappear?

### 4. What is the measure missing?

-   Home vs. away, and games that needed a flight across the Pacific (`venue`, `travelled_over_ocean`).
-   Opponent strength: 15 shots against the best defense is not 15 shots against the worst.
-   Red cards, corners, and anything else in the box score.

### 5. A hard cutoff or a probability?

-   A 0.5 margin turns xG into W/D/L. Why 0.5? How does accuracy change at 0.25 or 0.75?
-   Treat each team's goals as Poisson with mean xG and compute the probability of a win, draw, and loss. Use `games` here so each match counts once.

### Poisson-based Monte Carlo simulation

```{r}
library(dplyr)

set.seed(1) #means it is reproducible, every time the code chunk is ran it will give same answer
n_sims <- 10000 #10,000 simulations

# creates the real 2025 table: using points as the main way to decide order, then goal difference, then goals for
actual <- team_games %>%
  group_by(team) %>%
  summarize(pts = sum(points), gd = sum(goal_diff), gf = sum(goals_for)) %>%
  arrange(desc(pts), desc(gd), desc(gf)) %>%
  mutate(actual_pos = row_number()) # gives each team its acutal conference rank

# one row per real game (each game appears twice in team_games)
games <- team_games %>% distinct(game_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# has each team matching their position in the standings.
# will be used to keep track of each team's results during simulations.
home <- match(games$team,     actual$team)
away <- match(games$opponent, actual$team)

# Function simulates an entire season using expected goals (xG)

# row 2 and 3 randomly generate the number of goals scored in each game
# A Poisson distribution is used, with each team's expected goals as the average

# row 4-5 calculates the pointseach team should get based on the simulated score
simulate_season <- function() {
  gA <- rpois(nrow(games), games$xg_for)       # goals scored by the listed team
  gB <- rpois(nrow(games), games$xg_against)   # goals scored by the opponent
  ptsA <- 3 * (gA > gB) + (gA == gB)
  ptsB <- 3 * (gB > gA) + (gA == gB)
  who  <- c(home, away)                        # Combine results for both the home and away team so we can calculate total points, goal difference, and goals scored
  pts  <- rowsum(c(ptsA, ptsB), who)[, 1]
  gd   <- rowsum(c(gA - gB, gB - gA), who)[, 1]
  gf   <- rowsum(c(gA, gB), who)[, 1]          # calculate for all teams and use rowsum() to group the results by team
  pos  <- integer(13)                          # Create a vector to store the final position of each of the 13 teams
  pos[order(-pts, -gd, -gf, runif(13))] <- 1:13   # random coin flip if still tied
  pos
}

positions <- replicate(n_sims, simulate_season())   # 13 teams x 10,000 seasons
hit <- positions == actual$actual_pos                # TRUE = finished in its real spot

# 1) per-team results: real position vs expected position
actual %>%
  mutate(
    p_real_spot  = rowMeans(hit),
    avg_sim_pos  = rowMeans(positions),
    expected_pos = rank(avg_sim_pos, ties.method = "first")
  ) %>%
  select(team, actual_pos, expected_pos, avg_sim_pos, p_real_spot)


```

-   Westmont is the biggest loser from luck. Their xG says they should finish 8th, but they finished 12th, four spots lower. That matches their goal-difference gap of about −5 from earlier.

-   Vanguard, Dominican and Chaminade finished two spots higher than expected. Vanguard and Chaminade both conceded a lot less goals than their xG would predict

-   Concordia Irvine looks like they were unlucky to not make playoffs. They’re expected 3rd but finished 5th, one point behind Fresno Pacific for the last playoff spot.

```{r}
# how often a certain amount of teams hit the exact same positions, and the average amount of similar spots
table(colSums(hit))
mean(colSums(hit))

# how often the exact real table appeared
mean(colSums(hit) == 13)
```

-   Typical result: 1 or 2 teams land in their real spot (56% of seasons).

-   The average is 1.87 teams.

-   3+ teams land in real spot about 30% of seasons.

```{r}
library(dplyr)

set.seed(1)
n_sims <- 10000

# season simulation
simulate_season <- function() {
  
  #rpois simulation for goals using xG
  gA <- rpois(nrow(games), games$xg_for)
  gB <- rpois(nrow(games), games$xg_against)
  
  # points tally, 3 for a win, 1 for a draw, and 0 for a loss
  ptsA <- 3 * (gA > gB) + (gA == gB)
  ptsB <- 3 * (gB > gA) + (gA == gB)
  
  # makes one long list and uses rowsum() to add totals up by team. [, 1] pulls out the column of totals
  who  <- c(home, away)
  pts  <- rowsum(c(ptsA, ptsB), who)[, 1]
  gd   <- rowsum(c(gA - gB, gB - gA), who)[, 1]
  gf   <- rowsum(c(gA, gB), who)[, 1]

  # orders the team by points, most points higher in the standings, then tie breaks by goal different and then goals scored
  pos <- integer(13)
  pos[order(-pts, -gd, -gf, runif(13))] <- 1:13
  c(pos, pts)                       
}

# replicates the season 10,000 times, makes a matrix of each season as a specific column and 26 rows for the 13 positions and the 13 total amounts of points
sims      <- replicate(n_sims, simulate_season())

# Split the two halves back apart so they're easier to work with
positions <- sims[1:13, ]                           
points    <- sims[14:26, ]                       

#adds team names to rows
rownames(positions) <- rownames(points) <- actual$team

# position probability matrix 
# Row = team, column = finishing position, cell = P(probability that a team finishes in that spot)
# for each position j, positions == j is TRUE wherever a team finished in j position
pos_probs <- sapply(1:13, function(j) rowMeans(positions == j))
dimnames(pos_probs) <- list(team = actual$team, position = 1:13)

round(pos_probs, 3)   # full matrix

# summary of probabilities 
playoff_spots <- 4     # number of teams that make the playoffs

summary_probs <- tibble(
  team         = actual$team,
  actual_pos   = actual$actual_pos,
  # chances of winning the league
  p_win_league = rowMeans(positions == 1),
  # chances of making the playoffs
  p_playoffs   = rowMeans(positions <= playoff_spots),
  #chances of landing in the exact spot they were meant to finish in
  p_real_spot  = rowMeans(positions == actual$actual_pos)
) %>%
  arrange(actual_pos) # shown in a table

summary_probs
```

-   Everything is between 7% and 31%, where random guessing would be 7.7%. Westmont (7.2%) and Chaminade (8.7%) are very close to 7.7%, so guessing their position using xG does not help

```{r}
# uncertainty intervals
# runs quantile() on each speicific row (why the 1 is there) and asks for the the 5th, 50th, and 95th percentile in points and position
#t() helps flip apply() which originally has data in column form

q_pts <- t(apply(points,    1, quantile, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95)))
q_pos <- t(apply(positions, 1, quantile, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95)))

intervals <- tibble(
  team         = actual$team,
  actual_pos   = actual$actual_pos,  # where they really finished
  actual_pts   = actual$pts,    #the points they had
  xpts_mean    = rowMeans(points),    # average points across all 10,000 fake seasons. This is the xPoints number
  
  # the point  and position range: 5th percentile, median, and 95th percentile.
  # q_pts and q_pos has 3 columns, so [, 1] / [, 2] / [, 3] grab each one in order.
  # Together p05 and p95 give a 90% range, meaning 90% of simulated seasons
  # landed between them.
  pts_p05      = q_pts[, 1],
  pts_median   = q_pts[, 2],
  pts_p95      = q_pts[, 3],
  pos_p05      = q_pos[, 1],
  pos_median   = q_pos[, 2],
  pos_p95      = q_pos[, 3],
  
  # where the real points total falls in the simulated distribution
  # (near 0 = unlucky, near 1 = lucky or genuinely clinical)
  
  # For each team i, points[i, ] is its 10,000 simulated totals, and
  # actual$pts[i] is its real total. `points[i, ] <= actual$pts[i]` is TRUE
  # in every fake season where the team scored at or below its real points,
  # and mean() turns that into a share. So 0.95 means the team's real points
  # beat about 95% of the simulated seasons. seq_len(13) just loops over
  # the 13 teams. Because points are whole numbers, seasons that tie the real
  # total are counted too, so the percentile leans a bit high.
  actual_pts_percentile = sapply(seq_len(13), function(i) mean(points[i, ] <= actual$pts[i]))
) %>%
  arrange(actual_pos)  #show in real table order

intervals
```

-   For each team, `xpts_mean` is its average points across the 10,000 simulated seasons (its expected points), and `pts_p05` to `pts_p95` is the range that covers 90% of those seasons. `actual_pts_percentile` tells you where the real points total sits in that distribution, so 0.98 means the team beat 98% of simulated seasons.

-   Only two teams fall outside their 90% range, and that’s about what you’d expect. Point Loma’s 27 points is just above its upper bound (26), and Jessup’s 1 point is below its lower bound (3). With 13 teams and a 90% range, you’d expect roughly 1 team outside by chance, so 2 is not alarming. It does mean these two seasons were genuinely unusual. Everyone else is inside their range.

-   The table has three tiers by expected points:

    1.  Contenders (15.4–19.9): Point Loma, Hilo, Concordia Irvine, Vanguard, Azusa, Fresno and Menlo. All their `pos_p05` is 1.

    2.  Middle (10.7–12.5): Westmont, Biola, Hawaii Pacific and Dominican.

    3.  Bottom (5.3–8.0): Jessup and Chaminade.

-   Chaminade are in the bottom 4 in nearly every simulation (position range 10–13, median 13), but finished 11th. Their 8 points sit near the top of their range (95th percentile is 10).

-   Westmont and Jessup lost the most. Westmont’s range is 6–19 points, so 7 is near the bottom of it (10th percentile). Jessup’s real finish is at the extreme edge (2nd percentile).

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

playoff_spots <- 4
n_teams       <- nrow(actual)
cut_y         <- n_teams - playoff_spots + 0.5   # line between 4th and 5th

col_in   <- "#1b6ca8"   # playoff spots
col_out  <- "#b7c0c9"   # the rest
col_dark <- "#1f2933"

theme_table <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
        plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
        plot.subtitle      = element_text(color = "grey35"),
        legend.position    = "none",
        axis.title.y       = element_blank())

# The normal league table from the real games
actual_tbl <- actual |>
  mutate(label   = paste0(actual_pos, ". ", team),
         label   = fct_reorder(label, -actual_pos),   # 1st at the top
         playoff = actual_pos <= playoff_spots)

p_actual <- ggplot(actual_tbl, aes(pts, label, fill = playoff)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pts), hjust = -0.35, size = 3.8, color = col_dark) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cut_y, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  annotate("text", x = max(actual_tbl$pts), y = cut_y + 0.1, label = "Playoff line",
           hjust = 1, vjust = -0.4, size = 3.3, color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = col_in, `FALSE` = col_out)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Points",
       title = "Actual league table",
       subtitle = "Final standings, ordered by points, then goal difference, then goals for") +
  theme_table

p_actual

# The expected league table,, ordered by average points across the 10,000 simulated seasons (xPts).
# Bar = xPoints, whisker = 90% range, diamond = points actually earned.
expected_tbl <- intervals |>
  arrange(desc(xpts_mean)) |>
  mutate(exp_pos = row_number(),
         label   = paste0(exp_pos, ". ", team),
         label   = fct_reorder(label, xpts_mean),
         playoff = exp_pos <= playoff_spots)

p_expected <- ggplot(expected_tbl, aes(y = label)) +
  geom_col(aes(x = xpts_mean, fill = playoff), width = 0.72) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = pts_p05, xmax = pts_p95), height = 0.28, color = col_dark) +
  geom_point(aes(x = actual_pts, shape = "Actual points"), size = 3.2,
             color = "#d1495b", fill = "#d1495b") +
  geom_text(aes(x = pts_p95, label = sprintf("%.1f", xpts_mean)),
            hjust = -0.4, size = 3.6, color = col_dark) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = cut_y, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = col_in, `FALSE` = col_out), guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = c("Actual points" = 18)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Points",
       title = "Expected league table (xPoints)",
       subtitle = "Bars: average over 10,000 simulated seasons. Whiskers: 90% range. Diamond: real points.") +
  theme_table +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_expected
```
